atoms.name: Fresh ephemeral one-shot agent turn
atoms.statement: Each agent turn must be a new, ephemeral, non-resumed agent process whose only authority is the repository plus canonical harness state.
atoms.mechanism: run_once launches `codex exec --ephemeral --cd <root> PROMPT` with stdin=/dev/null and a fixed prompt naming repository/T1 state as sole authority; no session, resume or output-file arguments.
atoms.threat: Hidden conversational or session continuity steering work or acting as completion authority.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: one `omp -p --mode json` process per turn with no session continuation; the harness composes the prompt from repo state.

atoms.name: Fail-closed canonical integrity preflight
atoms.statement: Before and after every turn the harness must re-derive state and abort unless the ledger is ready with no pending recovery, plan and ledger agree, issues are empty, task ids are unique, at most one task is active, and every task contract is anchored to its latest registration receipt.
atoms.mechanism: _observe in both adapters checks build_report schema/ledger_integrity/plan_ledger_consistency/issues, duplicate or ambiguous active tasks, current_task consistency, contract-unregistered state, and per-task contract_registered/contract_update_accepted anchors.
atoms.threat: Acting on corrupted, ambiguous or silently edited plan/ledger state.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 recomputes state itself before and after trusting any turn.

atoms.name: Durable-delta progress snapshot
atoms.statement: A turn counts as progress only when a harness-computed snapshot (source digest, task contract/status/criteria/verification fields, ledger seq and tail hash) differs before vs after the turn.
atoms.mechanism: _snapshot builds a tuple before launch and again after an 'active' classification; equality downgrades the result to no_durable_progress (exit 11).
atoms.threat: Agent claiming progress without durable change; idle turns burning budget.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: progress is a harness-observed diff, never an agent statement.

atoms.name: Observed state outranks agent exit code
atoms.statement: Turn outcome is classified from re-observed canonical state; the agent exit code may only turn a still-active task into agent_failed and never creates or cancels a terminal state.
atoms.mechanism: _classify derives complete/blocked/active from the post-turn report first; a nonzero exit matters only while status is still active; 'interrupted' is mapped only from agent_failed. The selector likewise checks canonical deltas before exit codes.
atoms.threat: Trusting agent self-report (exit 0 = done) or losing a real completion because the agent crashed afterwards.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: core evidence-only rule.

atoms.name: Completion only when receipt-bound
atoms.statement: A task may be reported complete only if its projection is complete with valid history, an explicit completion binding, an integer authoritative receipt seq, and no current task.
atoms.mechanism: _classify 'complete' branch; anything else is protocol_error completion_not_receipt_bound.
atoms.threat: Plan text edited to 'Status: complete' without a verification receipt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: completion must point at a harness-recorded verification receipt.

atoms.name: Task identity fixed across a turn
atoms.statement: The task observed after a turn and reported by every child must equal the task that was active (or selected) before it; identity drift is a protocol or canonical error.
atoms.mechanism: _classify checks the starting task and current_task; the supervisor compares selected_task_id, each child's task_id and the re-observed active task.
atoms.threat: Agent swapping or re-registering tasks to escape a failing one.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Single typed result line per runner
atoms.statement: Each runner prints exactly one compact sorted-key JSON line with a closed key set and a typed outcome whose exit code is a fixed function of the outcome; agent output goes to stderr and unexpected exceptions become typed internal errors, never tracebacks.
atoms.mechanism: _emit in every runner; child agent stdout redirected to stderr; fixed EXIT maps; main() catch-all emits canonical_error internal_<Type>; the driver asserts its own line is <=1024 bytes.
atoms.threat: Agent output spoofing harness results; ambiguous or secret-leaking failure output.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: with omp --mode json, keep harness verdicts on a channel separate from agent events.

atoms.name: Precondition-gated zero-write launch
atoms.statement: An adapter must not launch the agent or mint a nonce unless its precondition holds (active task for execution; no active task and a valid goal for selection; agent binary present); otherwise it returns a typed not-applicable/unavailable result without writes.
atoms.mechanism: run_once returns no_active / not_applicable / codex_unavailable before snapshot or launch; the selector validates the master goal before secrets.token_hex.
atoms.threat: Wasted or unattributable agent runs; double selection after a crash.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Selection turn may only register
atoms.statement: Task selection is a separate agent turn that may only register a task: source digest, git tree, non-canonical residue and protected files (goal, AGENTS, active adapter) must be byte-identical across it.
atoms.mechanism: _snapshot records source/tree/residue/protected hashes; _residue_digest hashes every top-level entry plus .harness entries except plan/ledger files; _immutable_error compares before/after.
atoms.threat: Selector implementing work, planting files or hidden hand-off notes during 'selection'.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: enforce with omp tool_call filtering plus before/after hashing.

atoms.name: Per-invocation nonce binds the registration
atoms.statement: Each selection run mints a 128-bit random operation id, injects it into the prompt, and attributes a registration only if the new contract contains exactly one line `SELECTION_OPERATION_ID = <id>`.
atoms.mechanism: secrets.token_hex(16) appended to PROMPT; _selection_operation_id requires a single containing criterion with an exact fullmatch; mismatch gives selection_operation_unbound.
atoms.threat: Pre-staged, replayed, concurrent or externally written registrations being credited to this turn.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: inject via before_agent_start; generalize to bind any agent-produced artifact to the run that produced it.

atoms.name: Closed delta grammar for selection
atoms.statement: A selection turn's canonical delta must be either nothing or exactly one new task: prior tasks unchanged, plan append-only, ledger +1 contract_registered with matching id/hash/allowed paths, and the new task sole-active and unprogressed; anything else is protocol_error.
atoms.mechanism: _selection_error checks new-id count, historical task equality, plan prefix, receipt count and fields, sole-active, zero progress and allowed_paths; run_once rejects other changes as unsupported_canonical_delta.
atoms.threat: History rewrite, multi-task registration, pre-progressed or pre-verified tasks.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Deterministic contract lint at selection
atoms.statement: A selected contract must carry six non-vague justification fields, a terminal-property effect, a specific objective, <=8 non-root allowed paths, risk and out-of-scope lines, 6-40 criteria, 1-8 in-scope artifacts, a deterministic verify command and stop conditions, and must not add supervisors, routers or queues.
atoms.mechanism: _allowed_paths and _contract_error regex/length checks (vague words, giant task, supervisor/routing objective, hidden queue fields, forbidden path segments).
atoms.threat: Vague, unbounded or self-expanding tasks; smuggled task queues.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the structural bounds; regex vagueness checks are gameable hygiene, not evidence.

atoms.name: Normalized fingerprint blocks duplicate selection
atoms.statement: A new task whose normalized identity fingerprint (goal ids plus NFKC-casefolded gap/effect fields, excluding the nonce and WHY_THIS_TASK_NOW) equals any existing task's is rejected.
atoms.mechanism: _fingerprint hashes canonical JSON of the normalized IDENTITY_FIELDS; _selection_error rejects a fingerprint already in before['fingerprints'].
atoms.threat: Selection oscillation: re-selecting a blocked or finished task forever.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: exact-normalized match is evaded by rewording; add outcome- or artifact-overlap-based dedupe.

atoms.name: Goal completion derived, never declared
atoms.statement: Goal completion is accepted only from a completed final-verification task covering every terminal property whose current verification receipt seq/hash match its latest completion transition; registering nothing is never goal completion.
atoms.mechanism: _goal_complete (evaluate_completion require_current=True plus transition receipt binding); run_once returns protocol_error no_task_registered_goal_unproven when nothing is registered and the goal is unproven.
atoms.threat: Agent declaring the goal done, or idling at a no-active boundary.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: never trust omp goal-mode 'done'; derive goal completion from harness receipts.

atoms.name: Exactly one authoritative goal document
atoms.statement: Exactly one regular non-symlink master goal file may exist in the repository (outside .git), and it must pass the goal linter before selection or loop observation.
atoms.mechanism: rglob for T1_MASTER_GOAL.md must equal [goal]; master_goal_failures must be empty; lstat rejects symlinks.
atoms.threat: Shadow or duplicate goal documents steering selection; symlinked goal.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Bounded turn, episode and time budgets
atoms.statement: Work is bounded at every layer: at most 8 active turns per task episode, 32 episodes per loop, and finite nested wall-clock limits (6 h per child, 60 h per episode) whose inner budgets fit inside the outer ones.
atoms.mechanism: MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS, CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, MAX_SUPERVISOR_EPISODES, SUPERVISOR_EPISODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; cap hits emit turn_budget_exhausted / goal_loop_budget_exhausted.
atoms.threat: Unbounded loops, runaway cost, hung turns.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Consecutive no-progress stagnation stop
atoms.statement: Two consecutive turns without durable progress stop the episode as stalled_no_progress; a progressing turn resets the counter.
atoms.mechanism: consecutive_no_progress counter compared with MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NO_PROGRESS = 2.
atoms.threat: Spinning turns that never change durable state.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Effective-state oscillation detection
atoms.statement: Revisiting any previously seen effective-state fingerprint within an episode stops it as stalled_oscillation; the fingerprint covers task fields and source digest but excludes ledger seq/hash so repeated verification churn is not progress.
atoms.mechanism: _effective_fingerprint = sha256(canonical EFFECTIVE_KEYS + source_digest); a per-episode 'seen' set.
atoms.threat: A->B->A oscillation; re-running verification to look busy.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Supervisor re-derives progress itself
atoms.statement: After each child turn the supervisor recomputes effective state; a child claiming no progress while state changed is a protocol error, and a child claiming progress with unchanged state is caught as oscillation.
atoms.mechanism: observe() after every non-terminal child; current != previous on a non-active outcome raises child_progress_classification_mismatch.
atoms.threat: Buggy or tampered adapter misreporting progress.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every layer re-observes instead of trusting the layer below.

atoms.name: Strict child result validation
atoms.statement: A child's stdout is accepted only if it is <=1024 bytes of UTF-8, exactly one non-empty JSON line without duplicate keys or non-finite numbers, with the exact key set, a known outcome whose mapped exit code equals the real exit code, and typed bounded fields consistent with the outcome.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_child in the supervisor; _validate_supervisor in the driver adds object_pairs_hook/parse_constant and outcome-to-last-child consistency.
atoms.threat: Forged, truncated, smuggled or inconsistent child results.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Bounded nonblocking capture with deadline
atoms.statement: Child output must be read nonblocking with a hard byte cap (detecting cap+1) under a monotonic deadline; overflow or timeout aborts and the child's process group is killed.
atoms.mechanism: _read_available/_collect_child_stdout and _collect_supervisor using selectors with os.set_blocking(False).
atoms.threat: Infinite output, memory exhaustion, hangs on pipes held by descendants.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: apply to omp --mode json streams too (per-line and total bounds).

atoms.name: No automatic retry of failed turns
atoms.statement: Any typed failure (agent_failed, protocol_error, canonical_error, unavailable, interrupted) stops the episode and loop immediately; no runner retries a model turn or a launch.
atoms.mechanism: Stop on ERROR_EXITS in the supervisor; the driver returns on every non-complete supervisor outcome; source tests forbid retry/while surfaces in the adapters.
atoms.threat: Retry-until-pass masking failures; best-of-N cherry-picking.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Process-group cleanup on every exit path
atoms.statement: Every child runs in its own session/process group and is TERM'd, given a grace period, KILL'd and waited before its result is accepted, on success, error, timeout and SIGTERM alike.
atoms.mechanism: start_new_session=True; _cleanup_child/_cleanup_supervisor; _finish_supervisor always cleans before raising; _interrupt_on_sigterm turns SIGTERM into KeyboardInterrupt; cleanup failure maps to agent_failed.
atoms.threat: Leftover descendants mutating state after a verdict; orphaned agents.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 must own the whole omp process tree, including bash-tool children.

atoms.name: Single-flight supervisor lock
atoms.statement: Only one supervisor episode may run at a time; contention returns supervisor_busy without side effects and the kernel releases the lock if the holder dies.
atoms.mechanism: fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on the supervisor script's own inode; no pid or lock files.
atoms.threat: Concurrent episodes racing on one repository.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: lock the repository/state directory (as RUN-27 does), not the script inode.

atoms.name: Probe kernel supervision primitives before relying
atoms.statement: The loop driver must enable and read back PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, probe PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (set/verify/restore), confirm /proc lists itself, and give each child PDEATHSIG=SIGTERM with a parent-changed race check, failing closed if any primitive is missing.
atoms.mechanism: _load_prctl, _enable_process_supervision, and the _parent_death_preexec preexec_fn (exits 125/126) used by _start_supervisor.
atoms.threat: Assuming orphan cleanup works on a kernel or emulator where it silently does not; driver death orphaning an episode.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: Linux-only primitives, but probe-before-rely is a portable principle.

atoms.name: Reconcile adopted descendants to zero
atoms.statement: After each episode every descendant (including orphans adopted by the subreaper) must be found via a /proc ppid walk, TERM'd then KILL'd by group or pid, and reaped until none remain; no episode may start while any descendant exists.
atoms.mechanism: _process_parent_table, _episode_descendants, _reap_adopted, _signal_descendants, _reconcile_adopted_descendants; preexisting_adopted_descendant check at loop start.
atoms.threat: Detached grandchildren overlapping the next episode or mutating state after completion.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Repository guard lock with race check
atoms.statement: The driver holds a nonblocking exclusive flock on the repository's state directory, opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY and verified by dev/inode equality before and after open.
atoms.mechanism: _repository_guard context manager; contention yields goal_loop_busy.
atoms.threat: Two loops on one repository; symlink or rename swap of the state directory.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Re-verify terminal claims at the boundary
atoms.statement: A child's task_complete or goal_complete is only a hint: after all descendants are reaped the driver independently re-evaluates current receipt-bound completion (projection, current verification, latest transition seq/hash) and rejects stale or unbound claims.
atoms.mechanism: _current_task_completion and _current_goal_completion; failure yields canonical_error *_revalidation_failed.
atoms.threat: Stale terminal (a descendant changes an artifact after verification); forged child output.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the central evidence-only check; run it on omp session_stop.

atoms.name: Double-read stable observation for verdicts
atoms.statement: A completion verdict requires two consecutive observations to agree on root, ledger seq/tail, source digest, active task and plan tasks, and a repeated completion evaluation to return the same receipt.
atoms.mechanism: _stable_observation plus a second _observe and evaluate_completion inside the completion gates.
atoms.threat: TOCTOU with a concurrent or lingering writer during the verdict.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Observable state outranks transport errors
atoms.statement: After a child timeout or protocol error the driver re-observes canonical state and reports canonical_error if the repository is no longer observable, instead of the transport failure.
atoms.mechanism: _observe_after_transport on EpisodeTimeoutError/ProtocolError paths; a failed post-episode _observe maps to *_revalidation_failed.
atoms.threat: A crashing turn leaving corrupted state that is reported only as a timeout.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Stateless loop; repository is sole continuity
atoms.statement: Runner layers keep only process-local counters and persist no loop, pid or queue state; every episode and turn reconstructs from the repository and canonical ledger.
atoms.mechanism: In-memory LoopState; a fresh supervisor process per episode; per-run supervisor state dict.
atoms.threat: Hidden runner state becoming a second, unverified authority.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Strict layering of the runner stack
atoms.statement: The driver launches only the supervisor, the supervisor launches only the two adapters, only adapters launch the agent, and each layer is removable without canonical migration.
atoms.mechanism: _start_supervisor and the supervisor's call() invoke fixed scripts; source tests forbid direct model invocation above the adapters.
atoms.threat: Policy leaking across layers; untestable monoliths.
atoms.g1_hint: keep, but hash-pin the launched scripts (see findings).

atoms.name: Sterile per-run agent home
atoms.statement: A real-agent proof runs with fresh empty 0700 HOME/agent-home/TMP/XDG directories, an allowlisted environment without global git config, and only the approved auth plus a generated sanitized config admitted.
atoms.mechanism: _create_runtime_layout, _bootstrap_codex_home (exact entry set), _native_environment allowlist.
atoms.threat: Prior sessions, memories, caches or user config leaking context into a 'fresh' run.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: same pattern for omp's config/session/cache directories per run.

atoms.name: Reject provider redirection and continuity env
atoms.statement: Real-provider runs must refuse provider-redirect or fake-boundary variables and session/thread continuity variables, both inherited and in the constructed child environment.
atoms.mechanism: FAKE_NATIVE_ENV/CONTINUITY_ENV with reject_fake_native_environment; PROHIBITED_ENV_FRAGMENT in the per-invocation launcher.
atoms.threat: Silently testing against a fake or proxy provider, or resuming a prior session.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: map to omp provider/base-URL and session variables.

atoms.name: Pinned agent executable identity
atoms.statement: The agent binary must resolve to exactly one regular executable whose path, size and sha256 are recorded and version-checked, PATH-shadow checked at launch, and re-verified live by the offline verifier.
atoms.mechanism: _discover_native_identity; PATH re-resolution in _native_environment; load_spec identity hashes; _validate_native live comparison.
atoms.threat: Binary substitution or PATH shadowing by a wrapper.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: pin the omp binary/bundle hash.

atoms.name: Out-of-band /proc process trace
atoms.statement: Fresh-context claims are proven by the harness sampling /proc for descendants keyed by (pid, start_ticks): exe equals the pinned binary, argv is exec/--ephemeral/--cd fixture without resume/fork/session args, role comes from the ancestor script, and every process exited and was reaped.
atoms.mechanism: ProcessTracer.sample/finish polling every 10 ms; _assert_process_trace.
atoms.threat: Agent or adapter claiming freshness while reusing a session or long-lived process.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: combine /proc sampling with omp RPC/session events; sampling can miss short-lived processes.

atoms.name: Control repository unchanged by fixture run
atoms.statement: A proof run in a fixture must leave the control repository's canonical files, protected hashes, source digest and git tree byte-identical, checked live and re-checked by the verifier.
atoms.mechanism: _control_snapshot before/after (CONTROL_STATE_DRIFT); _validate_control requires before == after.
atoms.threat: A proof run contaminating the real repository.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Pinned protected-file hash inventory
atoms.statement: Harness control files are pinned by an approved sha256 inventory (plus an out-of-scope source digest) checked at preflight and by the offline verifier; any drift aborts.
atoms.mechanism: APPROVED_PROTECTED_HASHES, _protected_hashes, _validate_control_preflight; automatic E2E adds EXPECTED_PRIOR_HASHES and BASELINE_OUT_OF_SCOPE_SOURCE_DIGEST in _control_preflight.
atoms.threat: Agent or operator silently modifying harness code used by the proof.
atoms.g1_hint: keep, and extend it to the production loop's launched scripts.

atoms.name: Self-hash sealed evidence
atoms.statement: Evidence carries self_hash = sha256 of its canonical JSON with self_hash set to a zero sentinel; verifiers recompute it, and the written file is re-read and re-verified.
atoms.mechanism: evidence_self_hash/seal_evidence; verify_evidence_document before and verify_evidence_file after _write_new_json.
atoms.threat: Accidental corruption or partial writes of evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: a self-hash is not authenticity; anchor it in a harness-held key or ledger receipt.

atoms.name: Strict exact-key JSON parsing
atoms.statement: Evidence, specs and traces are parsed rejecting duplicate keys and NaN/Infinity, then validated with exact key sets at every nesting level.
atoms.mechanism: _exact_json_loads (object_pairs_hook, parse_constant) and _require_exact_keys in both E2E runners and the per-invocation launcher.
atoms.threat: Parser-differential and schema-smuggling attacks on evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Offline re-derivation verifier
atoms.statement: Evidence must verify offline with no provider by recomputing everything from embedded raw material: ledger hash chain, artifact bytes, manifest digests, receipt bindings, dependency values and trajectory frontiers.
atoms.mechanism: verify_evidence_document with _validate_fixture, _validate_raw_fixture_records and _validate_artifact_document; --verify-evidence reports provider_contacted false.
atoms.threat: Evidence checkable only by re-trusting the original run or its operator.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: One-shot attempt with typed failure evidence
atoms.statement: A real-provider proof gets exactly one attempt: pre-existing evidence blocks a rerun, a started attempt that fails writes sealed failure evidence to the same path, and failure evidence can never verify as success.
atoms.mechanism: existing_evidence_prevents_second_attempt / ONE_ATTEMPT_GUARD; _failure_evidence and _failure_document; success verifiers demand failure == None and the success key set.
atoms.threat: Best-of-N reruns cherry-picking a lucky success; failures disappearing.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: No secrets in evidence; credentials unrecorded
atoms.statement: Evidence and reports are rejected if they contain token/key/authorization-shaped strings, and credentials are recorded only by class, size and mode, never by content or digest.
atoms.mechanism: SECRET_PATTERNS/_scan_for_secrets on serialized evidence and reports; bootstrap admission records class/bytes/mode; the launcher trace excludes auth hashes.
atoms.threat: Credential leakage through evidence artifacts.
atoms.g1_hint: keep (regex scanning is heuristic in both directions).

atoms.name: Explicit non-claims in evidence
atoms.statement: Evidence must carry an exact, verifier-checked list of what is not proven (e.g. provider model identity configured-only, sampled /proc, unlink-not-overwrite, hook trust bypass used).
atoms.mechanism: LIMITATIONS compared verbatim; native E2E requires >=3 limitations and a fixed secure_removal_method; smoke records hook_trust_bypass_used and normal_trust_activation_proven=false.
atoms.threat: Overclaiming: evidence read as proving more than was observed.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Model text is never evidence
atoms.statement: Evidence and reports may not contain prompts, transcripts, response text, session/thread ids, raw model output or chain-of-thought; only harness-observed facts are recorded.
atoms.mechanism: Regex rejection of transcript/prompt/response_text/session_id/thread_id keys in verify_evidence_document; verify_report_structure forbids raw model output, chain-of-thought and session ids.
atoms.threat: Agent prose being laundered into authoritative evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: core paranoid rule.

atoms.name: Disposable genesis fixture for proofs
atoms.statement: Behavioral proofs run in a disposable fixture built outside the control repo from approved bytes, with a zero-task genesis ledger, empty git history and an asserted initial observation.
atoms.mechanism: _copy_fixture_source, _initialize_fixture_canonical_state, _git_init and _create_fixture expected-state checks; the automatic E2E adds manifest and git-object checks.
atoms.threat: Proofs contaminated by prior history, or polluting the real repository.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Cross-task dependency recovered from receipts
atoms.statement: A later task must recover earlier-task facts (artifact hash, verification receipt seq/hash, completion hash) from canonical ledger evidence and be registered after that completion; the verifier recomputes the binding and order.
atoms.mechanism: Fixture app build_b/verify_b; _collect_fixture_evidence expected_dependency; _validate_fixture order and distinctness checks.
atoms.threat: Hand-off via prompt or session instead of durable evidence; out-of-order tasks.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Context-identity chain per durable step
atoms.statement: Each durable step records the pinned-binary process identity (pid, start_ticks, exe sha256) that produced it, the previous step hash, a chain commitment, verified-dead predecessors and a pre-frontier; one context may produce at most one step.
atoms.mechanism: _current_native_identity walks /proc ancestry to the pinned exe; fixture_advance writes steps; _validate_step_values checks chain and distinct identities.
atoms.threat: One long context faking several 'fresh' contexts; step reordering.
atoms.g1_hint: experiment: useful for proving per-turn freshness on omp.

atoms.name: In-band claims cross-checked by observer
atoms.statement: An in-band step is accepted only if the out-of-band tracer independently observed the same live process identity, all predecessors were reaped with clean boundary scans, and no two active contexts overlapped.
atoms.mechanism: RotationTracer writes the observation trace and fails on ACTIVE_CONTEXT_OVERLAP; the fixture's _wait_for_observation/_validate_trace_for_task; the verifier binds trace to processes.
atoms.threat: Agent fabricating a context identity; overlapping contexts sharing memory.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep observer output in harness-private storage, not the agent workspace.

atoms.name: Frontier hash adjacency chain
atoms.statement: Each active context records pre/post frontiers (ledger seq/tail, plan sha, source digest, tree hash); consecutive contexts must be adjacent and an offline replay of step manifests must reproduce every frontier.
atoms.mechanism: _frontier/_frontier_valid; RotationTracer pre/post frontiers; _validate_frontiers replays manifests and checks adjacency and plan-hash changes.
atoms.threat: Hidden work between contexts; spliced or reordered trajectories.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a per-turn frontier chain is a cheap G1 trajectory proof.

atoms.name: Git-free tree hash re-derivation
atoms.statement: Verifiers recompute git blob/tree ids and the source digest from a file manifest without invoking git, and require the loose-object set and .git admin hash to match exactly (no packs).
atoms.mechanism: _manifest_entry, _manifest_source_digest, _tree_oids, _git_object_ids (zlib + sha1 per object), _git_admin_sha256.
atoms.threat: Hidden commits/objects as hand-off channels; trusting a possibly tampered git binary.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: worth it only if G1 must verify without trusting git.

atoms.name: Boundary scan for hidden channels
atoms.statement: At every context boundary the fixture's source paths, .harness paths, git admin hash, git object set and ignored caches must exactly match the expected stage, else CONTEXT_RESIDUE_PRESENT.
atoms.mechanism: _fixture_internal_scan with _expected_harness_paths, called pre- and post-context by RotationTracer.
atoms.threat: Notes, caches or git objects carrying context to the next fresh turn.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Disposable runtime root per invocation
atoms.statement: Every agent invocation gets a brand-new opaque runtime root (home, agent home, tmp, xdg, sqlite, rollout) created in an empty parent, never reusing a prior root id or inode, and deleted before the next invocation starts.
atoms.mechanism: _runtime_genesis (random id, inode-guard directory, empty children); _remove_runtime; lifecycle_records enforces cleanup_end < next genesis.
atoms.threat: Agent-internal databases or rollouts carrying context between 'fresh' turns.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: point omp's config/session/cache directories at a per-turn temp root.

atoms.name: PATH-interposed launcher wrapper
atoms.statement: The harness places its own launcher first on PATH under the agent's name so unchanged adapters' invocations are forced through exact argv validation (`exec --ephemeral --cd <fixture> <prompt>`, no continuation args) and isolation.
atoms.mechanism: launcher/codex symlink to run_per_invocation_native_runtime.py; _driver_environment path_boundary check; validate_adapter_argv.
atoms.threat: Adapters or agents invoking the agent outside the isolation boundary.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: on omp prefer SDK/RPC launch control over a PATH shim.

atoms.name: Guarded auth-file copy
atoms.statement: Only the approved auth file is copied: read O_NOFOLLOW, owner-only 0600, single link, bounded size, allowed JSON keys only (no context-bearing keys), written O_EXCL 0600 into the runtime; its source identity (dev, inode, size, mtime, sha256) must be unchanged at genesis and after the run.
atoms.mechanism: read_auth_snapshot, _validate_auth_value, _write_new_file, auth_unchanged; the spec pins source identity; the native E2E _approved_user_configuration rejects symlinked or group-readable auth.
atoms.threat: Credential tampering, token refresh written back to the real source, context smuggled through auth.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: same rules for omp's auth/token store.

atoms.name: Fresh pinned sanitized agent config
atoms.statement: Agent configuration is generated fresh per run from a pinned template (model, reasoning effort, tier, approval never, hooks/plugins/apps/multi-agent off) with its template hash recorded; no user config is inherited.
atoms.mechanism: CONFIG_TEMPLATE and CONFIG_TEMPLATE_SHA256 in the launcher; _minimal_config in the native E2E; the automatic E2E pins SANITIZED_CONFIG_BYTES.
atoms.threat: User config enabling plugins, hooks or providers that alter behavior or leak context.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: generate omp settings per run and pin model roles explicitly.

atoms.name: Syscall-entry write-boundary tracer
atoms.statement: The whole agent process tree is ptraced and every mutation-capable syscall is classified at entry by resolved target (runtime/fixture/device/nonpersistent/external); external targets or bypass syscalls (mount, ptrace, bpf, setns, untraced clone, ...) kill the tree before the syscall runs.
atoms.mechanism: trace_native_process with TRACEFORK/CLONE/EXEC/EXITKILL options; _pending_mutation, classify_write_target, BYPASS_SYSCALLS; aarch64-only, fails closed on other architectures.
atoms.threat: Agent writing outside its sandbox (real home, other repos) or escaping observation.
atoms.g1_hint: experiment: only on a real kernel; prefer landlock/bubblewrap/seccomp-notify enforcement over a Python ptrace observer.

atoms.name: Fd hygiene and io_uring denial
atoms.statement: Before exec the traced child starts a new session, sets PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL, closes all inherited fds >=3, sets NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs a seccomp filter returning ENOSYS for io_uring_setup so every write stays ptrace-observable.
atoms.mechanism: Fork-child block in trace_native_process; _install_io_uring_denial BPF program.
atoms.threat: Inherited writable fds or io_uring submissions bypassing entry-time observation.
atoms.g1_hint: keep if any syscall-level containment is attempted.

atoms.name: Emulated-ptrace syscall decoder fallback
atoms.statement: When PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO is unsupported (nested PRoot), syscall stops are decoded from aarch64 registers via GETREGSET with per-tracee entry/exit phase tracking, and the decoder used is recorded in evidence.
atoms.mechanism: _aarch64_syscall_registers; fallback_in_syscall map with fork-child phase setdefault; syscall_decoder field.
atoms.threat: Misdecoded syscalls under PRoot's partial ptrace emulation.
atoms.g1_hint: drop: nested PRoot ptrace cannot prove termination/reap (EXITKILL unimplemented); run on a real kernel or make no containment claim.

atoms.name: Exactly one pinned agent process
atoms.statement: Each invocation must observe exactly one process image of the pinned agent binary in the traced tree; zero or several is PROCESS_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS.
atoms.mechanism: native_identities collected from early stop probes and PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC as (tgid, start_ticks); len != 1 fails.
atoms.threat: A wrapper or substitute executing instead of, or alongside, the pinned agent.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: admit known self re-exec (tool helpers) or the rule self-defeats; currently untested.

atoms.name: Hash-chained lifecycle trace on fixed schedule
atoms.statement: Invocation lifecycles are appended as genesis/process/cleanup triplets to an owner-only, fsynced, hash-chained trace (seq, previous hash, run id) checked against a fixed role schedule derived from the parent adapter; partial, resealed, out-of-order, extra or wrong-role invocations fail, and an incomplete predecessor blocks successors.
atoms.mechanism: read_trace, validate_trace_groups, append_trace (O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW + fsync), SCHEDULE, _parent_role, role check in _runtime_genesis.
atoms.threat: Replayed or forged lifecycle records; surplus provider invocations.
atoms.g1_hint: keep, with the trace outside agent write reach (a plain hash chain is re-sealable by any writer).

atoms.name: No live references before deleting a root
atoms.statement: Before deleting a runtime root the harness must find zero mounts, cwd/root/fd/mmap references and AF_UNIX sockets into it across same-UID processes, and no symlink or hardlink crossing out of it.
atoms.mechanism: _mount_reference_count, _process_references, _artifact_taxonomy prior_crossings; failures raise PRIOR_RUNTIME_REFERENCE_PRESENT or GENERATED_RUNTIME_STATE_TRANSFER_DETECTED.
atoms.threat: Live processes retaining authority over 'deleted' state; links smuggling state out.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Continuity-bearing runtime artifacts forbidden
atoms.statement: Agent-generated artifacts that can carry context across invocations (sessions, threads, histories, memories, rollouts, sqlite stores, installation ids, mutated config, unknown files) must stay confined to the per-invocation root and be destroyed or rejected; unclassified means forbidden, and only byte-pinned markers may be admitted.
atoms.mechanism: RESIDUE_NAME, _runtime_scan categories A-D, INSTALLED_RUNTIME_FORBIDDEN_ARTIFACTS, _sandbox_migration_artifact; metadata-only counting in _artifact_taxonomy.
atoms.threat: Agent runtime databases or memories acting as a hidden continuity channel.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: enumerate omp's own session/memory stores and isolate them per turn.

atoms.name: TOCTOU-safe exact file reads
atoms.statement: Security-relevant files are read via lstat, O_NOFOLLOW open and fstat equality (dev, inode, mode, uid, gid, nlink, size), requiring a single link, the expected owner/mode and a size bound.
atoms.mechanism: _read_exact_regular; read_auth_snapshot; metadata checks in load_spec and read_trace.
atoms.threat: Symlink/hardlink swaps and concurrent replacement of files being verified.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Hash-pinned import of reused verifier code
atoms.statement: Verifier code reused from an earlier runner is imported only if the file's sha256 equals a pinned constant and the expected attribute surface exists.
atoms.mechanism: PRIOR_RUNNER_SHA256 check before importlib loading; REUSED_BASE_SURFACE hasattr check.
atoms.threat: Silently changed shared verifier logic weakening later proofs.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: No stale loop processes at preflight
atoms.statement: A run may not start while any goal-loop, supervisor, adapter, launcher or ephemeral agent process matching the exact argv shape is alive.
atoms.mechanism: _is_goal_loop_process over the /proc table in _control_preflight, raising PROCESS_RESIDUE.
atoms.threat: Leftover processes from an earlier run writing into the new run.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Provider-free scripted mock model
atoms.statement: Agent-runtime integration is tested against a loopback mock Responses server that issues scripted tool calls and records the tool outputs it receives, so command execution is observed at the transport instead of being narrated by a model.
atoms.mechanism: MockResponsesServer on 127.0.0.1:0 streams SSE function_call/message events and captures function_call_outputs and tool names; smoke_codex points a temporary config at it.
atoms.threat: Tests depending on a live provider, or trusting model narration of tool results.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: register a mock provider for an omp model role and assert on recorded tool_call events.

atoms.name: Real home and harness state unchanged
atoms.statement: An agent run must use an isolated temporary agent home and prove that the real home's stable config/auth files and the harness's canonical state bytes are hash-identical before and after.
atoms.mechanism: stable_codex_home_snapshot and t1_state_snapshot before/after; checks real_codex_home_unchanged, temporary_codex_home_isolated, hook_invocations_changed_no_t1_state.
atoms.threat: Agent runs mutating the operator's real configuration or the canonical ledger.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: snapshot omp's real config dir; note the snapshot skips volatile session/log/sqlite stores.

atoms.name: Strip root-redirect env and workspace PATH
atoms.statement: Child agent environments drop repository/git redirection variables (HARNESS_ROOT, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE) and PATH entries inside the workspace, and replace HOME/TMPDIR.
atoms.mechanism: isolated_child_environment; scrubbed_environment(runtime_dir, denied_root).
atoms.threat: Redirecting the harness at another repository or shadowing tools with workspace binaries.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Single allowlisted chat, silent drop
atoms.statement: The remote gateway acts only on updates whose chat id equals the single configured id and silently ignores every other chat.
atoms.mechanism: SAFE_CHAT validation in Config; Gateway.handle_update compares chat.id (bools rejected).
atoms.threat: Unauthorized Telegram users triggering agent jobs; oracle responses to probers.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: also allowlist the sender user id (a group chat id admits every member).

atoms.name: Bot token never leaves the gateway
atoms.statement: The bot token must never appear in repr, errors, child environments, results or chat: errors are redacted with exception chains suppressed, the child env drops TG_* and any value containing the token or chat id, results are redacted, and raw agent diagnostics are withheld.
atoms.mechanism: field(repr=False); TelegramClient._redact and `from None`; CodexRunner.child_environment; _redact_exact_values; generic failure messages.
atoms.threat: Credential leakage via tracebacks, logs, the agent environment or chat messages.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Remote jobs refuse full-access sandbox
atoms.statement: Remotely triggered agent runs may only use read-only (default) or workspace-write sandboxing; danger-full-access is a configuration error.
atoms.mechanism: TG_CODEX_SANDBOX check in Config.from_environment; CodexRunner.command passes --sandbox.
atoms.threat: A remote message granting unrestricted host access.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: map to omp tool permissions/approval policy.

atoms.name: Bounded validated attachments
atoms.statement: Attachments must match strict file-id/path/media-type patterns (no traversal), agree on declared, getFile and downloaded sizes under a 20 MB cap, be materialized 0600 in a job-private temp dir with a sha256, never be auto-extracted, and be deleted after the job.
atoms.mechanism: parse_attachment, _valid_attachment_size, TelegramClient.get_file/_file_url/download_file, materialize_attachment, TemporaryDirectory in JobController._work.
atoms.threat: Path traversal, oversized or size-shifting downloads, archive bombs.
atoms.g1_hint: keep if G1 exposes a remote channel.

atoms.name: Durable ack before side effect
atoms.statement: The next update offset is durably persisted (temp file, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync; 0600 file in an owner-only directory outside the repo) before an update is dispatched, so a crash never replays a job.
atoms.mechanism: OffsetStore.prepare/load/store; run_loop stores the offset and then calls handle_update; _validated_update_ids sorts and rejects bad ids.
atoms.threat: Duplicate job execution after a crash or restart; offset tampering through the repo.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: at-most-once for any externally triggered job.

atoms.name: One cancellable job at a time
atoms.statement: The gateway runs at most one agent job, launched without a shell in its own process group with the prompt on stdin and a wall-clock timeout; cancel or timeout terminates the whole group TERM then KILL.
atoms.mechanism: JobController.submit/cancel/shutdown; CodexRunner._run_once and _terminate_group.
atoms.threat: Job pile-up, shell injection via argv, orphaned agents after cancel.
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Content-free progress reporting
atoms.statement: Remote progress is derived only from event types and counts in the agent's JSONL stream, never from event content, with per-line and total log size bounds.
atoms.mechanism: ProgressLogReader._describe/consume with MAX_EVENT_LOG_BYTES and MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES.
atoms.threat: Leaking code, secrets or model reasoning to a remote channel.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: map from omp --mode json event types.

atoms.name: Same-model retry; no silent model switch
atoms.statement: Provider capacity errors may be retried only with the same model, with bounded exponential backoff inside the job deadline; exhaustion is reported explicitly and the model is never substituted.
atoms.mechanism: MODEL_CAPACITY_ERROR detection on the diagnostic tail; CodexRunner.run retry loop (<=5 retries, delay <=300 s).
atoms.threat: Silent downgrade to a different model invalidating evidence assumptions.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: pin omp model roles and record the model actually used.

atoms.name: Gateway preflight and fail-closed config
atoms.statement: Before polling, the gateway validates token shape, a real git repository root, absolute non-symlink state/temp paths outside the repo, bounded numeric knobs, the agent binary on PATH, a bot identity and the absence of a webhook.
atoms.mechanism: Config.from_environment, OffsetStore.prepare, preflight() and main().
atoms.threat: Misconfiguration placing harness state inside the agent workspace, or competing update consumers.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: harness state must live outside the agent-writable workspace.

findings.detail: _kill_tracees leaves its reap loop on ChildProcessError (or after 5 s) without proving every tracee is gone, then run_one's finally rmtree's the runtime root while tracees may still hold cwd/fd/map references (the PRoot report reproduces this); kills here and in _signal_descendants use bare pids with no start-ticks revalidation.

Tracer false-positive aborts: utimensat is always decoded as (dirfd, path), but futimens() (used by touch, cp -p, os.utime(fd)) issues utimensat(fd, NULL, ...), so _read_cstring(0) fails with bad_pointer; _read_cstring also pread()s fixed 256-byte windows, so a path ending within 256 bytes of an unmapped page short-reads and aborts the run.

The exactly-one native identity rule appends every PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC of the pinned binary, so any self re-exec (e.g. via the arg0 helper symlinks apply_patch/codex-linux-sandbox that _artifact_taxonomy explicitly admits as pointing at the native binary) yields native_count_2 and aborts; no test covers the count check.

Write-boundary gaps: classification happens at syscall entry while sibling threads keep running, so path buffers and symlinks can change after inspection inside the traced tree (LIMITATIONS only disclaims races outside it); persistent kernel objects such as SysV IPC (shmget/msgget/semget) and keyrings are absent from the syscall tables.

Why runtime isolation is blocked: under nested PRoot 5.1.107, PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO returns ENOTSUP, PTRACE_O_EXITKILL is accepted but not applied, detach drops signals and resume failures are hidden, so a selector agent pair stayed in tracing-stop (PROCESS_REAP_UNPROVEN) and the reap remediation was blocked pending a real-kernel topology; meanwhile the E2E agent config is danger-full-access with approval never, relying on exactly this boundary (the gateway refuses that mode).

Why the automatic fresh-context E2E is blocked: installed Codex writes continuity-capable state into CODEX_HOME (.sandbox_migration marker, goals/logs/memories/queue/state sqlite, installation_id sent as request metadata, workspace-trust config mutation, skills tree), failing first the boundary scan (CONTEXT_RESIDUE_PRESENT) and then the pre-provider gate (FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME_ARTIFACTS_PRESENT).

_native_admissions_valid and INSTALLED_RUNTIME_TEMPORARY_ARTIFACT_ROOT are unreferenced; _installed_runtime_semantic_gate is unreferenced, fails unconditionally and is stale (docstring/proof say 0.151.0 but it compares to EXPECTED_NATIVE_IDENTITY 0.152.0); _runtime_boundary_scan, _validate_initial_runtime_scan, _validate_marker_trajectory and build_blocked_evidence run only from tests.
In _collect_child_stdout the conditional `if eof or not _child_group_exists(process.pid): break` is followed by an unconditional break, so the condition and its killpg probe are redundant.

_predecessor_binding makes byte-equality with /sdcard/(removed)/t1/draft/ report copies a hard preflight requirement, contradicting AGENTS.md: external draft copies are never required and must not assume a host-specific path.

_validate_supervisor hard-codes maxima 8/2/9 instead of deriving them from the supervisor's MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS/MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NO_PROGRESS, so changing a cap silently turns valid results into protocol errors.

_goal_ids counts any standalone 'T1' (the project name) or 't1-' task-id prefix as terminal property T1/P01, so ordinary prose can spuriously satisfy terminal coverage in goal-completion checks and fingerprints.

At a no-active boundary the selector requires scripts/run_fresh_turn.py as a protected artifact (canonical_error if absent), but the 'deleting the active adapter leaves the selector functional' test only exercises the active-task early return.

The production driver and supervisor re-launch supervisor/adapter scripts (which re-import codex_harness) from the target repository every episode with no hash pin, so an active turn can rewrite the code that judges later turns; only completion claims are independently re-verified, while blocked/stalled/error outcomes are accepted as reported.

The supervisor's single-flight lock is its own script inode, so a copied supervisor on the same root bypasses it (disclosed P4); simultaneous external SIGKILL of driver and supervisor leaves detached adapters alive (disclosed).

A self-hash is integrity, not authenticity (anyone can reseal); only externally pinned hashes protect evidence, and the blocked-evidence verifier accepts self-attested pytest/ruff 'pass' values, test counts and red-team verdicts it cannot reproduce.

The gateway authorizes a chat, not a sender (every member of a group chat id can run jobs); the agent stderr log is unbounded; child_environment strips any variable whose value merely contains the chat-id digits, which for a short id would drop PATH/HOME.
smoke_codex.py executes `raise SystemExit(main())` at module level with no __main__ guard, so importing it launches a real agent run.

E2E proofs are single-scenario and host-bound (hard-coded ledger seqs 260-274, a fixed uid, absolute nvm paths, exact model); /proc evidence is 10 ms sampling with task attribution inferred from episode index; the observer trace is written into the agent-writable fixture.

run_fresh_turn and run_no_active_selection have no timeout of their own, and subprocess.run kills only the direct child on interrupt, so standalone use is unbounded and can orphan agent descendants; bounds and group cleanup come only from the supervisor.
